newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-BHP rated long-term buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-BHP rated long-term buy.

text.p: Brokerage J.B. Were and Son has rated Australian resources group The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) a long-term buy but says the near-term outlook is clouded by forecasts for lower copper and oil prices.

In a research report sent to J.B. Were clients last month, the brokerage forecast the copper price to fall to 85 U.S. cents per pound for BHP's business year ending May 1998, compared with an estimate of 97 cents for 1996/97.

"The immediate outlook for BHP remains clouded by potentially falling copper and oil prices, however, longer term, BHP is getting set for substantial earnings growth through its raft of new projects," the report said.

BHP has an estimated A$7.5 billion worth of new projects under construction or in the pipeline, it said. "These new projects will add around A$850 million by 2000 to BHP's yearly base earnings of A$1,300 million," the report added.
Lower copper and oil prices over the next six months will probably depress BHP's share price, leading perhaps to buying opportunities, the report said.
The report was prepared when BHP's share price stood at A$17.78, well above its closing price at A$17.12 on Tuesday. The stock ended last week at A$16.78.
At A$17.78, it said the shares appeared overvalued and recommended clients take an underwight position in the short term. BHP comprises 9.5 percent of the Australian market.
